headline: Approved five-unit residential project at 2001 Kingstown Road and a one-year extension for Greenhouse Dispensary; continued Peacedale Preserve zoning change to September 8.
summary: The Greenhouse Dispensary extension was requested because the state's license lottery was put on hold and will now be held in January 2027. Members raised many concerns about the Peacedale Preserve proposal, including storage units, cabins, and an event center, and the item was continued.
decisions: Approved a one-year extension of the Greenhouse Dispensary approval, now expiring December 16, 2027.
Approved the preliminary plan for a five-unit residential project at 2001 Kingstown Road by unanimous vote.
Continued the Peacedale Preserve zoning map and text amendment to September 8, 2026.

decision_evidence.quote: The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves a one-year extension to the December 16, 2025, approval of the Special Use Permit for a Marijuana Retail Facility and Preliminary Plan for the Greenhouse Dispensary Minor Land Development project, now expiring December 16, 2027.

The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the application for Preliminary Plan approval for the 2001 Kingstown Road Multi-Household Minor Land Development Project for a five (5) unit residential development located at 2001 Kingstown Road, Wakefield, RI also identified as Assessor's Plat 32-4, Lot 21. ... passed by unanimous vote.
This application was continued to September 8, 2026 (no vote).

decision_titles: Five-unit residential project at 2001 Kingstown Road
Peacedale Preserve Special Management District zoning amendment
plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Planning Board   
Regular Session Agenda Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 6:30 PM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
Maria H. Mack, Chair 
Susan Axelrod, Vice Chair 
Elizabeth Karp, Secretary 
Paul Jordan 
Robyn Pothier 
Kaiper Wilson 
Armand Monaco 
 
A. Call to Order & Roll Call: 
Ms. Mack called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. 
 
ROLL CALL: 
Present:  Susan Axelrod, Paul Jordan, Liz Karp, Armand Monaco, Robyn Pothier, Kaiper Wilson, and Maria Mack. 
Absent:  None 
 
Also Present: James Rabbitt, Director of Planning; Brian Wagner, Deputy Director of Planning; Curtis Dufour, Principal 
Planner; Lynn Smith, Planning Associate; Mark Conboy, Town Engineer; and Peter Skwirz, Special Legal Counsel. 
B. Approval of Minutes: 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Wilson, passed unanimously. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the listed meeting minutes, as presented."  
 1. July 21, 2026 PBWS Minutes 
 2. July 28, 2026 PBRS Minutes 
C. Subdivisions and Land Development Projects: 
 1. EXTENSION REQUEST: Greenhouse Dispensary - Minor Land Development Project with UDR request for 
extension of Preliminary Plan approval. 
Kenneth Tetzner, applicant, appeared to present the application.  Mr. Tetzner explained that due to the State of Rhode 
Island being sued by three out-of-state entities and ending up in Federal Court, the State of RI put a hold on the lottery 
system for license distribution.  The bill has been re-written, and the lottery will now be held in January 2027.  Due to 
the fact that the Preliminary Plan approval expires in December 2026, an approval extension is being requested. Mr. 
Skwirz advised the board to follow the one-year extension practice that is used for other types of applications. 
 
The following motion, made by Ms. Wilson, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, passed unanimously. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves a one-year extension to the December 16, 2025, 
approval of the Special Use Permit for a Marijuana Retail Facility and Preliminary Plan for the Greenhouse Dispensary 
Minor Land Development project, now expiring December 16, 2027. 
 2. PUBLIC HEARING:  2001 Kingstown Road - Minor Multi-Household Land Development Project to demolish 
an existing single-family home and develop the property with one duplex structure and one triplex structure 
(e.g. 2 structures containing 5 total units). Located at 2001 Kingstown Road, Wakefield; Assessors Plat 32-4, 
Lot 21. Ashworth Investments, LLC owner/applicant. (Continued from June 23, 2026) 
Jeff Caffrey, of Resnick and Caffrey, 300 Centerville Road, Warwick, RI, attorney for the applicant, appeared to present 
the Preliminary Plan application.  Mr. Caffrey informed the board that after speaking to Mr. Rabbitt, Director of 
Planning, they now have a better plan; Mr. Caffrey described the changes.   
 
Mr. Conboy stated that his comments, outlined in his July 28, 2026, memo to Mr. Rabbitt, can be addressed at the 
permit level for the storm water soil erosion and runoff permit.
Mr. Rabbitt spoke regarding the property being in the special management district; and the applicant's willingness to 
adjust the architecture.  Mr. Rabbott put the new architecture on the screens. 
 
Discussion ensued regarding the new color scheme; any landscaping changes; the architectural layout of the building is 
the only change; stonewall shown in the front is to be repaired and preserved;  
approve the site plan with modified architecture; "substantial" compliance and not "complete" compliance with 
submitted architectural plans. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT:  None 
 
The following motion, made by Ms. Karp, duly seconded by Ms. Pothier, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: “The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby closes the PUBLIC HEARING: 2001 Kingstown Road — Preliminary 
Plan, Minor Multi-Household Land Development Project." 
 
In addition to the items listed in the August 25, 2026, Project Review Memo, Mr. Rabbitt added two items: 
#9 The applicant shall submit final architectural renderings that are consistent with architectural renderings submitted 
by planning department staff on August 8, 2026, and made part of the record as it relates to the duplex and triplex 
exterior fenestration and color palette.  #10 The applicant shall add a detail to the site plans depicting the reconstruction 
of the stone wall, including dimensions and material. Final details shall be reviewed and approved by the AO 
(Administrative Officer). 
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Wilson, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the application for Preliminary Plan approval for the 
2001 Kingstown Road Multi-Household Minor Land Development Project for a five (5) unit residential development 
located at 2001 Kingstown Road, Wakefield, RI also identified as Assessor's Plat 32-4, Lot 21.  Ashworth investments, LLC, 
applicant.  The approval is based on the following materials: Finding of Fact 1A - E; and Condition of Approval 1–10." 
D. Development Plan Review: 
None. 
E. Recommendations to Town Council: 
 1. ZONING MAP AND TEXT AMENDMENT — "The Peacedale Preserve Special Management District." 
Application to amend the Town's Zoning Ordinance to create a new zoning district identified as Tax 
Assessor's Map 33, Lot 30; Property being designated for new or expanded commercial, residential and 
recreational land usage. Applicant/owner BWJW, LLC, 371 Rose Hill Road, Wakefield, RI  02879. 
Patrick Dougherty, attorney for the applicant, appeared to present the application along with Ed Pimentel and Molly 
Titus. 
 
Mr. Pimentel reviewed the changes made as a result of the information and guidance provided by the board at the last 
meeting.   
 
Mr. Rabbitt added, as mentioned, this is a Special Management District (proposed). There are multiple layers to this 
proposed district. Such as an existing outdoor shooting range and an existing indoor shooting range. The text 
amendment and map change are requesting four additional components be added. (1) The rental type units, whether 
they be called short-term rentals or time-shares, in a cottage-like setting; (2) a sports kind of clubhouse; (3) a wedding 
venue; (4) an autominium, which includes boats stored indoors, wine collections, and other types of art collections. No 
contractor storage, no mini storage and no outdoor storage are permitted in association with those units. The last thing 
is residential development. 
 
Mr. Rabbitt gave a breakdown of the proposed map/text amendment, explaining the changes that would be triggered by 
adding a residential development.
Ms. Mack stated that it may be useful to get a sense of how board members feel.  
Ms. Mack requested to hear from other planning board members. 
 
Discussion ensued with the Planning Board expressing concern with: one-acre house lots; more compact development; 
single-family, duplex, multifamily, and flexible frontage design; enforceable conditions on approval; asking for a lot; 
event space along with rentals in a specific location on the site; guardrails added for events; concern with addition of 
residential space to event space; no problem with existing sporting events built upon; concern with lack of background 
information for the site; no information on restrictions for the previous approval of the indoor gun range; no 
information on site constraints, although adjacent to a super fund site; potential soil contamination from lead; cabins 
and wedding condos, although transient, are residential units; number and potential scale of certain items such as 
condos and the difficulty in enforcement of those; term of "upscale flexible" storage units is not defined and 
enforcement will be uncertain; too much being requested for the site; 70 storage units too high a limit; confusion 
regarding proposed zoning; unclear delineations in zoning request; not comfortable with the zoning request and not 
clear in thinking these uses are permitted on the entire 122 acres; conservation land easements along the riverbank; 
Pavilion will have solid walls; Pavillion poorly described; volume of light and noise from open windows; signage; 
proposed amendment's reference to Rt. 1 Special Management District guidelines regarding signage incorrect; two 
items from the Comprehensive Community Plan not met "future commercial and industrial development must not 
overwhelm the unique character of the community" and "high quality of life for our residents", not aspirational with 
Comp Plan;traffic concerns for Rose Hill Road; concerned about the size of the upscale storage units, how many acres of 
impervious surface will those storage units be; no mention of the other storage unit totaling 17,000 square feet;why not 
ask to rezone the portion of property you want to develop now; too many different elements, too many different 
elevations, don't feel they go together; concern with the extensive requested uses; objection to the two different 
concepts of the event center and pickleball; supportive of the vision for the property, not supportive of the zoning 
ordinance request before them; need to set a maximum number on the storage units and the cabins; no commercial 
uses north of the existing indoor range; concerned about nonresidential uses scattered within the 120 acres; concerned 
about noise and traffic associated with an event center; concerned about no limitation or minimal limitations on 
residential density with gun operations still in place; concerned about the reference to commercial size zoning, signage, 
in a residential zone; concerned about the density without any restrictions on conservation or open space;  
 
Ms. Mack spoke regarding the comments made by the project team regarding "coming back to the Planning Board for 
Master and Preliminary approval", however, if the zone change is approved, anything in the future will be "by right." 
  
Mr. Rabbitt stated that the Planning Board could make a recommendation to the Town Council that non-residential 
components of this zone can not be located X number of feet from the southern boundary of the zone, in order to 
confine that nonresidential development to the area being shown conceptually, minus the total amount of storage units 
of seven. Mr. Rabbitt advised the Planning Board could structure a recommendation to the Town Council that the non-
residential components have a limited area within the 120 acres; pick that dimension based on the conceptual plan with 
some flexibility of them being able to provide utilities. Mr. Rabbitt stated the Planning Board would be able to make a 
recommendation to council limiting the commercial development of the 120 acres of this particular zone to a portion of 
the property.    
 
Ms. Mack stated that there is not a great deal of comfort from this board with regard to this proposal.  Two ways to 
proceed: One is that it could be modified, to have a greater degree of comfort from the Board.  It could be withdrawn, or 
we could vote on this, and then you would proceed to the Council regardless of what the outcome would be.  
 
Mr. Dougherty stated that he would like the board to vote and, add conditions that you have talked about here, as a 
backup of any consideration.  If the council were to go forward and adopt this, we would like X,Y and Z.  Just so you 
could give respect to the comments made here. Mr. Dougherty spoke of the effort, detail, and his client's vision and 
respectfully asked that the board vote. 
 
Ms. Mack stated that she appreciates the level of detail gone to; however, there is no guarantee based on what is 
currently in this draft, be this or another applicant, that would necessarily be the way it would go forward, because of
the lack of restrictions within the text.   
 
Mr. Rabbitt advised the Board, if a negative recommendation is given without backup,it does not give much guidance to 
the next decision-making board, being the Town Council, if they were to entertain adopting the regulation.  When it 
goes to the Town Council, the Town Council will ask staff what were the concerns of the Planning Board.  Even if you 
make a negative recommendation, put a caveat on that if the Council were to entertain any aspect of this, we would 
appreciate you: 
1. restricting the non-residential components of this text amendment to the southern portion of the site, based on the 
conceptual plans presented to the planning board.  
2. eliminate the event center, which needs to be consensus by the board. 
3. limit the density of the residential space until all gun operations are gone.  Per staff's recommendations.   
4. Reduce the signage to the character of the neighborhood verses referring to another commercial zone in town. 
5. Require a percentage of the land utilized,,to be planned residential, to be set aside as open space or conservation 
land, density on less acreage and more land or conserved. 
This gives a little bit of guidance to the council if, in any instance, they are going to entertain moving forward with this.  
 
Ms. Mack stated that with any negative recommendation the board would be happy to articulate the reasons why and 
what the issues that we see would be with this, rather than just a blanket no and that may give some guidance going 
forward, or it may create a different sort of application. 
 
Mr. Jordan asked if a positive recommendation could be crafted tonight, 4 nays, 3 yays. 
 
Mr. Dougherty agreed to a two-week extension. 
 
Mr. Skwirz addressed the 4 no-votes citing the statute that sets forth the precedents for approvals for projects like this 
one. 
 
Mr. Rabbitt read and summarized the compiled list of concerns. 
 
Mr. Dougherty, yes, agrees to a two-week extension. 
  
Mr. Skwirz commented on special use permits. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT: 
Dane Ardente, Esquire, attorney for the Frisellas, appeared to voice objections to the proposed map and zone 
change. Mr. Ardente expressed concerns, including the wedding function use/special use permit requirement with 
objective criteria re. notice levels and parking. 
 
This application was continued to September 8, 2026 (no vote). 
 
 2. Old Tower Hill Road Neighborhood Project, Form-Based Code: Review and Recommendation to the South 
Kingstown Town Council. 
Mr. Rabbitt referenced the draft letter and the Form Based Code passed out to the Planning Board members at the 
beginning of the meeting.  
The Planning Board members were requested to send comments to Jame Rabbitt by Tuesday with recommended 
changes. Mr. Rabbitt informed the board of the newspaper ad for the Public Hearing, beginning to run this week. 
Mr. Wagner reminded the Planning Board members of comments made by Mr. Teitz at the Planning Board Work 
Session. 
F. Reports and Special Items:
1. Review of Draft Update to S.K. Wastewater Facilities Plan - Discussion and possible action on 
recommendation to Council. 
Richard Bourbonnais, Director of Public Services, appeared to explain the need to appear.  Every 5 years the Facility Plan 
for the Town's Waste Water System. Partners with Narragansett and URI.    Potential expansions discussed.  
 
Consultant explained the two elements of the Facility Plan, a 20-year plan. 
Presentation was made on Chamber screens. 
G. Report of Administrative Officer: 
None. 
Ms. Mack and planning board members expressed their displeasure with the current PB electronic packets being 
distributed through the Agenda software. 
 
Ms. Mack would like to work on the Rt. 108 special management district.   
 1. Decision of the Administrative Officer in accordance with RIGL. 
None reported. 
H. Designation of Duty Member for Next TRC Meeting: 
Mr. Jordan volunteered to attend the September 9, 2026, TRC meeting at 9:00 a.m. 
I. Adjournment: 
Upon Motion made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Axelrod, the meeting was adjourned at 9:11 p.m., by 
unanimous vote.
